title: opum-workflow SessionEnd hook creates a self-sustaining tracker-chore PR loop
summary: The SessionEnd (and PreCompact) hook body in hooks/flush-state.sh always dirties the working tree: step 2 unconditionally rewrites .claude/handovers/cursor.md, and step 1 appends a boilerplate implementation note ('Session <reason> at <ts>. Branch <b>, N uncommitted file(s)...') to the tracker whenever exactly one task is In Progress -- regardless of whether the session actually did anything. Under opum-sdlc, a dirty tree needs a branch and a PR to land. Landing that PR ends a session, which fires the hook again, which writes another note and dirties the tree again. The loop is self-sustaining: no human or model input required to keep it going.

acceptanceCriteria.text: State the loop's actual trigger precisely: which of (a) the cursor rewrite (untracked/modified file every run) and (b) the tracker note (only when exactly one task is In Progress) is doing the dirtying in each observed case, since the fix differs depending on which one is load-bearing.

Design and ship a fix in opum-workflow's flush-state.sh (or the surrounding hook contract) that stops boilerplate-only commits/PRs from being generated, without losing the ability to reconstruct session state that the hook exists to provide -- see the design options opum-agent raised: skip the tracker note when nothing changed since the last note, or move it to the cursor (already the non-durable, discarded-on-read half of the handoff) instead of the tracker.

Confirm the fix does not reintroduce the original defect flush-state.sh was written to fix -- the lore-cli predecessor hook produced an EMPTY handover for a session that read, searched and reasoned without editing a file, because it derived state only from a PostToolUse checkpoint. A 'skip when nothing changed' rule must not silently drop a substantive but edit-free session the same way.
After the fix ships and at least one full session-end cycle has run against it, confirm no new boilerplate-only tracker-chore PR was opened, and that a real substantive note still lands durably.

implementationNotes: Filed by opum-agent (orchestrator), 2026-09-09, from evidence in lore-web: their last five commits (#71-#75) are ALL 'chore(tracker): commit session-renewal note', and LWEB-55 carries 12 implementation notes of which 9 are hook boilerplate, burying the 3 substantive ones -- so the cost is not PR noise, it is a task record whose signal is diluted to a quarter by its own tooling. opum-agent's own OPAG-64 shows the same pattern at smaller scale: 6 of its last 8 notes before 2026-09-09 were boilerplate.

Design framing from opum-agent, offered as a starting point rather than a ruling: the flush deliberately writes the tracker BEFORE the cursor because the tracker is the durable one (survives a discarded working tree / rebuilt machine) and the cursor is explicitly non-authoritative and discarded on read (see opum-handoff skill). This bug is a case of the durable channel being used to carry the least durable content -- a per-session heartbeat with no decision, reasoning, or handoff value on its own once the note is one of a run of identical ones.

INTERIM INSTRUCTION already given fleet-wide by opum-agent, in force until this ships: nobody opens a PR whose entire content is one of these boilerplate notes. Let it ride along uncommitted or bundled into the next substantive commit instead. This stops the loop without a code change while the fix is scheduled.
